text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.55% today as Brent crude oil broke through $116 a barrel—a six-month high—driven by escalating Middle East tensions and U.S. threats of military action against Iran. The company benefits directly when oil prices rise, since it earns more revenue per barrel produced. The broader energy sector has rallied nearly 12.5% over the past two weeks as geopolitical risk premiums pile onto crude, with analysts flagging oil majors as plays on the "next leg" of this energy trade.

The setup reflects a structural shift in global energy markets: as Middle East conflict threatens oil supply and disrupts traditional trade routes, U.S. energy producers—especially those with diversified operations like ConocoPhillips—stand to gain from both higher prices and new demand for alternatives like liquefied natural gas from allies like Qatar seeking to avoid Iran-dependent suppliers.
